correctness.rationale: Every first-layer submodule is a unique inverse image of an L-subspace. The free-type versus exotic distinction follows from the S-trace. The centralizer computation extends isomorphisms to GL2(F); absence of a k-linear relation at nonrational t forces integral entries and equality of lattice indices forces unit determinant. This proves equivalence with PGL2(k) orbits. Stabilizer orders 1, q+1, and q(q-1) for high-degree, quadratic, and rational points respectively yield the class-size formula. The standalone finite-field checker agrees in seven cases, but arbitrary q,d are proved symbolically.

value.rationale: The first radical layer is the natural smallest finite classification problem surrounding the recent non-iso-Artinian square example. The exact number and multiplicities of abstract module-isomorphism types expose the structure of its exotic submodules and show rapid growth with residue degree; the integral isomorphism criterion is essential and not a relabeling of a known orbit table.
